newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's president in TV appearance after illness.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's president in TV appearance after illness.

text.p: Vietnam's President Le Duc Anh and a hardline former politburo member made surprise television appearances on Friday, months after both had disappeared from public view because of ill-health.
Evening broadcasts showed General Anh, 76, who suffered a stroke in mid-November, smiling and in apparent good health as he talked with fellow members of Vietnam's elite politburo.
Hours earlier, Anh issued his first public statement since being admitted to a Hanoi hospital more than two months ago, saying he was recovering.
A brief despatch, carried by the official Vietnam News Agency, quoted Anh as saying he wished to thank people who had sent messages of concern during his illness.

"The illness is now over. My health is in the process of recovery. On behalf of my family and myself I would like to sincerely thank everyone, and would like to send my best wishes to all the people, cadres and friends," he was quoted as saying.
VNA added that senior members of the elite politburo had met Anh on Friday and expressed the hope he would be well enough to return to work soon.
Anh, the most powerful military figure in Vietnam, is a member of the nation's leadership triumvirate alongside Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi and Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet.

He had initially been admitted to hospital following problems related to high blood pressure. It later became apparent he had suffered a stroke, but within hours a veil of secrecy was drawn across details of his health.
Widely conflicting reports made accurate assessment of his condition difficult, but diplomats said at the time he was unlikely to return to work.

Aside from a passing reference to Anh's absence from a state function in November, Friday's statement and television appearance marked the first significant recognition by Vietnam's state-controlled media that the head of state had been ill.

Just moments after President Anh's appearance, state television followed with the first pictures in months of hardline former politburo member, Dao Duy Tung, being presented with an award for 50 years membership of the ruling party.
Tung, 67, disappeared from the political scene last May in the run up to a major Communist Party Congress.
On Friday, he looked bloated and with a vacant expression on his face. Prior to his appearance, it had been rumoured he was seriously ill, or even dead.
The public emergence of both men comes just days before Vietnam's Tet Lunar New Year festival, which runs from February 6 to 10, and is the most important holiday of the year.

Although Hanoi will wish the development to be portrayed as a sign of leadership unity at an auspicious occasion, it is likely to be the focus of considerable speculation by Vietnam watchers over the political ramifications.

Analysts had linked Dao Duy Tung's illness to fallout from the earlier expulsion from the politburo of a disgraced senior politician, Nguyen Ha Phan, who was removed from office amid allegations of treason.
The two men had been considered allies.
